motion: Can God's existence be established through contingency, religious experience, or moral obligation?

con.label: The arguments do not establish God

lockedRoutes.description: Establish God through a necessary ground of contingent existence, reinforced by the best explanation of religious experience and the objective authority of moral obligation.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: Show that at least one argument supplies a warranted bridge from the relevant experience or contingent reality to a transcendent personal ground identifiable as God.

motionBridge.description: The cumulative arguments warrant affirming that God exists.

centralBridges.description: Contingent beings require an external and ultimately necessary ground.
Mystical experience is best explained by an objective transcendent cause.
Objective moral obligation requires a transcendent ground of value.

subsidiaryBridges.description: A total explanation cannot terminate solely in unexplained contingent members.

lockedRoutes.description: Defeat establishment by challenging the intelligibility and scope of metaphysical necessity and by supplying non-divine explanations or underdetermination for experiential evidence.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: Show that each offered route either relies on an unjustified conceptual extension or leaves live rival explanations that prevent the asserted inference to God.

motionBridge.description: None of the proposed routes establishes the existence of God.

centralBridges.description: Necessity and causal explanation do not validly extend to a necessary being.
Private religious reports do not discriminate God from rival mental causes.
Moral obligation and judgment admit non-divine explanatory accounts.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Observed effects and sincere reports remain compatible with false beliefs.

lockedSections.title: Contingency and necessary existence
lockedSections.rationale: This exchange states the principal metaphysical proof and the foundational objection to applying necessity to a being.

lockedSections.title: Meaning of metaphysical terms
lockedSections.rationale: The parties clarify contingency, necessity, and existence, determining whether the principal inference is even expressible.

lockedSections.title: Explanation of the totality
lockedSections.rationale: This section tests the decisive transition from explanations of members to an explanation outside the whole series.

lockedSections.title: Religious experience
lockedSections.rationale: The competing moves test whether mystical experience discriminates an objective divine cause from rival reported experiences.

lockedSections.title: Moral obligation
lockedSections.rationale: The final route asks whether the distinctive authority of moral obligation requires God or permits an environmental account.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frederick Copleston
lockedMoves.proposition: Because contingent beings lack their own sufficient reason, their totality requires an external existent ground that ultimately cannot fail to exist.

lockedMoves.speaker: Bertrand Russell
lockedMoves.proposition: Necessity applies significantly only to analytic propositions, so a necessary being would require an existence denial that is self-contradictory.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frederick Copleston
lockedMoves.proposition: A contingent being lacks the complete reason for its existence, whereas a necessary being must exist and cannot fail to exist.

lockedMoves.speaker: Bertrand Russell
lockedMoves.proposition: The proposed necessary being collapses into an ontological claim, but existence is not a predicate and cannot be analytically affirmed of a named subject.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frederick Copleston
lockedMoves.proposition: The series is either caused or uncaused; because an uncaused series would be self-sufficient and necessary despite wholly contingent members, it must have an external cause.

lockedMoves.speaker: Bertrand Russell
lockedMoves.proposition: Searching successfully for particular causes does not imply universal causation or warrant expecting the world as a whole to have an explanation.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frederick Copleston
lockedMoves.proposition: Mystical awareness of a transcendent object is not strict proof, but its basic character is best explained by an objective cause rather than a wholly subjective account.

lockedMoves.speaker: Bertrand Russell
lockedMoves.proposition: Equally convinced reports concern demons and other rejected entities, so recorded mystical conviction does not establish that its alleged divine object exists.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frederick Copleston
lockedMoves.proposition: Widespread consciousness of moral law and obligation is best explained by a transcendent, non-arbitrary ground of value and author of the moral law.

lockedMoves.speaker: Bertrand Russell
lockedMoves.proposition: The sense of moral ought can arise from imagined disapproval, customs, taboos, environment, and education rather than from a transcendent lawgiver.
